text:
anya: Quick sanity check — ran a staging perf sweep after the kernel handoff change and seeing odd batching shapes for 8k prompt clients. p99 jumps on mixed workloads.
sam: Which kernels were selected? Did selector flip to the new matmul-v2 path or stay on the fallback?
anya: It was oscillating. kernel_selector picked matmul-v2 for long sequences but then fell back to sparse-optim for some shards. KV hit rate dropped ~15% during flips.
kai: Can you paste the queue/admission policy config? I suspect the continuous groomer is merging short chats into long batches which is increasing decode contention.
anya: Here's the admission snippet we used for the run:
```
queue_policy: groomer
batch_formation: continuous
token_budget_targets:
  short: 64
  mid: 256
  long: 1024
decode_rate_buckets: [fast, medium, slow]
kernel_affinity: disabled
```
sam: That mid token_budget feels low for clients with slow decode rates. If decode-rate is slow, continuous batching keeps them in the head and pushes other clients back — increasing tail latency.
matt: Also worth checking KV cache churn. If kernel switch picks a larger tile it can expand KV footprint and cause extra evictions. Any eviction metrics?
anya: kv_eviction snapshot during spike:
- evict_rate: +22% at 13:14 UTC
- avg_kv_age: 240ms -> 90ms
- kv_hit_rate: 78% -> 66%
perf-bot: probe run 2026-03-15T13:14Z: summary: p50 +3.2%, p95 +6.1%, p99 +11.7% (vs baseline)
kai: Proposal: make token_budget a function of decode-rate. e.g. budget_map = {fast:32, medium:128, slow:512}. This reduces per-batch token mass from slow decoders and prevents them from dominating batch formation.
sam: And add a kernel_affinity hint on the classifier: prefer matmul-v1 for mid lengths when decode-rate == slow to keep KV working set smaller. We should avoid hard forcing but use affinity score.
anya: Starting a 30-min canary with new budgets + kernel_affinity_hint enabled. Will record batch_size histogram, kernel_choice histogram, kv_hit_rate, and p99.
matt: Also add an admission quota cap per client to stop a single long-decoder from starving the microbatch pool. small cap like 8 concurrent in-flight reqs per client.
anya: ACK. Canary started at 13:30 UTC. Running synthetic mixed workload: 60% short (<=512 tokens), 30% mid (512-2048), 10% long (>2048).
perf-bot: canary finished: p99 -7.8%, p50 -1.9%, mean_batch_size -3.1%, kv_hit_rate +9.4%, kernel_stability (percent of time selector stayed on primary kernel) +18%
sam: Nice win. Need to confirm no regression for pure-long workloads; schedule a follow-up baseline test with 100% long.
kai: If follow-up looks good, let's wire token_budget mapping into the classifier DAG and expose a tunable override in console.
anya: Opening PR with the changes and a test harness for mixed workloads. I'll attach the canary artifacts.
matt: Add a short doc blurb on why token_budget scales with decode-rate — helps debugging when someone sees reduced batch sizes.
anya: Will do. Summary saved to artifacts: /ops/artifacts/groomer-canary-2469123456.tar.gz :thumbsup:
perf-bot: note: schedule automated regression check in 24h window for GPU kernel change set.
anya: thanks all, will follow up once the PR lands and post the perf dashboard link.
